messages.subject: Cholesky decomposition with pivoting?
parts:
[moved to stan-dev]

On 11/25/13, 2:11 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> On Monday, November 25, 2013 12:35:13 AM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
>
> On 11/25/13, 12:32 AM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
>
> > The cholesky_decompose function in Stan does not use pivoting and hence that L is calculated very inaccurately with
> > Sigma is singular. That is why I suggested to calculate L in R with pivoting.
>
> Is there a way we can make what we're doing more robust
> by pivoting. As you know, my linear algebra fu is weak,
> at best.
>
> It shouldn't be hard to change the behavior, as it's
> a simple function that's already unit tested.
>
>
> Well, with pivoting it permutes the rows and columns, so it would lead to a lot of user errors. We do use the 3-factor
> Cholesky with pivoting internally in some case.
>
> Basically, for fixed covariance matrices, you can do the decomposition externally and pass it as data. Or you could do
> it in Stan via an eigendecomposition instead of the Cholesky decomposition. In the parameterized case, everyone would be
> better off working with the Cholesky factor primitive types.

I take it that this means we get the same degree of error
if we unpivot (?) back to a regular Cholesky factor? That is,
the user would need to use the pivoted solution and pivot to
get decent accuracy?

I want to prioritize getting the Cholesky factor for correlation
matrices into Stan --- it shouldn't be that hard and I finally
understand how useful it'll be!

- Bob
